title: Art Tatum's technique
summary: Carter calls Tatum a sacred cow who dazzled and moved him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I'm thinking of ... let me call one name into question, and that's Art Tatum (PIANISTIC) for example, who I think a lot of people might say that his facility or his technique often tended to play itself in a fashion; that is, that he had such a command of the instrument that many patterns and so forth, simply fell under his fingers, and that the technique more often expressed itself or was used as an expression of itself than really being at the command, perhaps, of musical ideas, which, if he had less technique or command of the instrument, he might have been more thoughtful about some of the things he was playing.
Are you asking me if I agree with that?
I don't know. I guess it's almost like -- Tatum to me is almost like a sacred cow, I guess that's what -- what does that mean, like when I say a sacred cow, what does that mean?

Like Untouchable? Yeah, I don't know -- it's very hard to criticize anything that he did. When he came on the scene, he was such a blockbuster. I mean, no one had heard anything like Tatum. And like I heard a musician, as I had mentioned probably in an earlier part of this interview, Monroe Burger -- that I heard -- someone had asked me to go hear, and after I listened to a few sets and we left, he said, 'What did you think of him' and I said, 'He dazzled me, but he didn't move me.'
But that was because he had tremendous technique, but, you know, kind of, as we call it, little 'soul'.

But Tatum dazzled me and moved me, and I think he did to a lot of people. Now, I also know, on the other side of the coin, there are any number of people who said Tatum played too much for them, and I think that's what you were referring to.
Yes, but I don't know -- I guess I am kind of prejudiced on his behalf, you know? To me he could do no wrong. Whatever he did was just fantastic to me.
Okay. Well, we'll keep him safely enshrined.
